subject: Nordbank — DPA + subprocessor list request
related_links: Drive (gated): Redwood Trust Pack / DPA + Subprocessors
body:
From: Marta Nowak <marta.nowak@nordbank.eu>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 09:43:12 +0100
Subject: Nordbank — DPA + subprocessor list request

Hi Lukas,

As part of our procurement process, we need the following documents to proceed with the vendor onboarding:

1) Your current Data Processing Addendum (DPA), incl. any Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) you rely on
2) A list of all subprocessors relevant to the services (incl. cloud providers / infrastructure)
3) Confirmation on how we are notified of subprocessor changes

If you have a canonical location where these are maintained, please point us there (we want to avoid stale versions).

Thanks,
Marta

—
Marta Nowak
Vendor Management & Procurement
Nordbank


From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Nowak <marta.nowak@nordbank.eu>
Cc: Jonas Berg <jonas.berg@nordbank.eu>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 11:02:38 +0100
Subject: Re: Nordbank — DPA + subprocessor list request

Hi Marta,

Thanks — understood.

Attaching:
- Redwood_DPA_Template_v2025-12.pdf (our standard DPA template)
- Redwood_Subprocessor_List_2026-01.pdf (current list as of this week)

On canonical versions: we maintain these as part of our Trust Pack. For external distribution, we provide the latest approved PDFs (like attached) and can re-send an updated copy anytime you’d like to confirm the current version.

Subprocessor change notification: for material changes we provide advance notice to customers (typically via email notice to designated security/procurement contacts) and offer an opportunity to raise objections consistent with the DPA.

If you share your preferred signatory details, I can initiate signature on the DPA once your legal team confirms the template is acceptable.

Best,
Lukas

—
Lukas Meyer
Account Executive, EMEA
Redwood Inference


From: Jonas Berg <jonas.berg@nordbank.eu>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marta Nowak <marta.nowak@nordbank.eu>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 15:27:09 +0100
Subject: Re: Nordbank — DPA + subprocessor list request

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for sending.

A couple of clarifications from our privacy team:

- Does your DPA incorporate SCCs (EU Commission 2021/914) and, if so, which module(s)?
- For Hosted / Dedicated (if applicable), do any subprocessors process data outside the EEA by default?
- How do you handle subprocessor updates in practice (lead time / where notices are sent)?

If you have standard language for these items, please share.

Regards,
Jonas

—
Jonas Berg
Privacy Counsel
Nordbank


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jan 2026 09:11:04 +0000
Subject: Re: Nordbank — DPA + subprocessor list request

Lukas — below is approved standard language you can forward to Nordbank (feel free to paste verbatim).

SCCs:
Redwood’s DPA includes the EU Commission SCCs (2021/914) as an optional annex for cross-border transfers, where applicable. The specific module(s) and annex details are completed based on the customer’s contracting entity and the deployment model.

Data location / transfers:
Data processing location depends on the deployment model and the customer’s configured region(s). Where customers select EU regions for hosted services, Redwood will process customer content in the selected region(s) except as necessary for limited operational metadata and support, and subject to the subprocessors listed in the current subprocessor list. Redwood will not represent that customer data never leaves a region in all circumstances; the DPA and subprocessor disclosures govern.

Subprocessor changes:
Redwood maintains a current subprocessor list and provides advance notice of material changes to designated customer contacts. Customers may raise reasonable objections in accordance with the DPA.

Important: please avoid committing to a specific number of days lead time unless Nordbank asks for a contractual term. If they do, loop Legal/Security for review.

— Aisha
